chunks: And in the narration of al-Sakuni, it was reported to ʿAli عليه السلام:
“A man had relations with his father’s wife, so he stoned him, while he was not muhsan.”

key_terms.امْرَأَةِ أَبِيهِ: his father’s wife; a prohibited marital relation
key_terms.غَيْرَ مُحْصَنٍ: not muhsan; not legally in the state that ordinarily entails rajm for zina
key_terms.فَرَجَمَهُ: so he stoned him; imposed the hadd punishment of rajm

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man who commits zina with his father’s wife according to Imam ʿAli عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Imam ʿAli عليه السلام concerning a man who had intercourse with his father’s wife. It indicates that the punishment imposed was stoning, even though the man was not muhsan, showing the grave legal status of this prohibited act in Shia fiqh.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5045 - In the narration of Al-Sakuni, it was reported to Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) that
a man had committed fornication with his father's wife, so Imam (as) ordered him to be stoned, even though he was not married (non-muhṣan).
